questions.question: A bag holds 5 red, 3 blue and 2 yellow marbles. Find the probability of each colour, show that the probabilities add to 1, and find the probability of not blue in two ways.
questions.expected_answer: Ten equally likely marbles. P(red) = 5/10 = 1/2, P(blue) = 3/10, P(yellow) = 2/10 = 1/5. Sum: 5/10 + 3/10 + 2/10 = 10/10 = 1. P(not blue) = 1 − 3/10 = 7/10, or directly by counting the 5 red and 2 yellow: 7 over 10.

questions.question: A die was rolled 60 times with frequencies 8, 11, 9, 12, 10 and 10 for the faces 1 to 6. Check the total, and find the relative frequency of a 4 and of an even number. Explain why the denominator is 60.
questions.expected_answer: Total: 8 + 11 + 9 + 12 + 10 + 10 = 60 rolls. RF(4) = 12/60 = 0.2, or 20 percent. RF(even) = (11 + 12 + 10)/60 = 33/60 = 0.55. The denominator is the number of trials, 60, because relative frequency is the fraction of the trials in which the outcome happened, not the number of possible outcomes, which is 6.

questions.question: A spinner game at a school fun day has 8 equal sectors, one of which wins a prize. 240 learners play once each. Predict the number of prizes and the prize budget at R15 a prize, and explain why the class should buy a few extra prizes.
questions.expected_answer: P(win) = 1/8, so the expected number of prizes is 1/8 of 240, which is 30. Budget: 30 × 15 = 450, so about R450. The expected frequency is an average, not a guarantee: the actual number of winners varies around 30, and 26 or 35 winners would be ordinary, so a few spare prizes protect against a run of luck.
